MMM.rationale: MMM is a deteriorating business with sharply negative earnings trajectory, expensive valuation, and significant legal/structural headwinds. Q1 2026 showed revenue +1.3% YoY but EPS collapsed -39.7% YoY and -20.6% QoQ, with net income down -41.3% YoY. Operating cash flow plunged -826.6% YoY to just $574M. The balance sheet is severely strained with total equity of only $3.31B against $32.12B in liabilities (debt-to-equity ~3.8x). P/E has expanded from ~18.7x a year ago to 29.1x today despite earnings deterioration, and P/B sits at 24.6x near the top of its 365-day range (17.1-25.0). Net margin has compressed from 17.9% to 11.2%. The Solventum spin-off removed the higher-margin healthcare business, leaving a more cyclical industrial portfolio. Ongoing PFAS litigation with 30+ state AG cases and personal injury suits creates unpredictable cash outflow risk. Rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.45%) and elevated oil prices ($92.65/bbl) add macro headwinds for industrials. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to reverse the negative trajectory. The stock is paying peak multiples for declining earnings power.
